title: Filter rail + tabbed dashboards: five ways to do it in data-ui
kicker: /babble 5 · case study: all four UR5e trajectory datasets, 212 trajectories
brief: Your Nov 24 ask: "this general pattern that should be supported in data-ui is like multi tab dashboards, where you filter the data that is included in the dashboards with a left hand bar … this will happen again and again! so please show like 5 different ways". The case: trajectories as the atomic unit, Dataset as the first filter, dev/holdout applying across every dataset ticked, tabs that feel like switching dashboards, and a component compact enough to drop into any app. All five are live prototypes on the same 212 trajectories, built on the vendored data-ui, each checked full page and inside a fake host app's 1000 × 680 slot.
defaultWhy: P1 · Workbench element scores 98/100: one tag, <data-workbench src="coverage.base">, gives the TensorBoard layout inside its own box (rail, a tab strip at the element's top, a pill row of the active filter on every tab), fits the 1000 × 680 slot with all six tabs and a 196 px rail, and another app reuses it with only its own .base. Its weak spot: it is one fixed layout; an app that wants the parts elsewhere (a card, a side pane) can't rearrange them, which is exactly P5's strength. The build I'd do: P5's <data-scope> as the core, P1's workbench as its default layout, and P4's colour-by-dataset in every figure.
decisionHinge: The criteria never reward laying the same parts out differently per app. If that matters (a card in robotparts, a pane in Clank, Obsidian's sidebar), P5's scope is the right API and P1 becomes its default layout rather than the API. Second hinge: if comparing datasets matters as much as the filter itself (FR6 at 25, taken from "drops into any app"), P1 and P4 tie at 95: P4's one-row-per-dataset maps and numbers are the best comparison of the five.
invariants: The same 212 trajectories (four UR5e datasets at full speed) from one analyze() payload; every figure re-aggregates exactly from membership.json (extract.py asserts it, and P2–P5 re-check at load).
Same figures (round 2's V2 occupancy engine) so the container pattern is what differs; same viewport (1440 × 900), same host slot (1000 × 680), same check (check.cjs, 7 gates).
Dataset is the first filter in every proposal, and split applies across every dataset ticked.
boundary: Live prototypes in traj_compare/docs/proposals/dashboard-pattern-2026-11-24/ on the vendored data-ui (main 2f08a88); each proposal's new data-ui API is a prototype in its own folder, nothing is in data-ui yet. Open in Rerun really launches Rerun through traj_compare.serve. The pictures here are captures of those prototypes.

variants.name: Workbench element
variants.thesis: One new data-ui element, <data-workbench src="coverage.base">, owns the whole pattern inside its own box: the rail, a tab strip of dashboards along the element's top (not the page's), and the dashboards; the .base declares the rows, the rail and pages:.
variants.bestWhen: Most apps want the same layout (TensorBoard without the app bar) and should get it from one tag plus a .base, the way robotparts or Vibe Tracks would.
variants.losesWhen: An app wants the parts arranged differently (a card, the filters in its own sidebar); a selection made on one page doesn't carry to the next; the prototype wraps the stock dashboard's drill to add Rerun and keep ‹ › on the filtered rows.

variants.name: The rail holds the tabs
variants.thesis: One left column does both jobs, like VS Code's or Linear's sidebar: the dashboards as a list on top, the filters under them; the main pane is only the active dashboard, and below 1100 px the column folds to an icon strip.
variants.bestWhen: Space is tight (a pane in Clank, a narrow embed): it is the most compact of the five, a 48 px strip plus the dashboard.
variants.losesWhen: You want the tab feel you asked for: dashboards are a vertical list, and folded they are icons with tooltips; changing a filter in the strip takes one extra click.

variants.name: Every tab is a saved view
variants.thesis: data-ui almost has this already: one <data-views> over the trajectories, a <data-facets> rail, and every dashboard is a saved view of a new type: panels — so the tabs are data-ui's own view tabs, + adds your own, and the filter is the one every view already shares.
variants.bestWhen: You want the smallest change to data-ui and user-made dashboards: + in the bar adds a dashboard tab, and "Save as tab…" keeps the current subset as its own tab.
variants.losesWhen: Embedded with the rail open the bar shows 4 tabs + "2 more…"; panels can't be dragged or resized yet; the status line repeats the count.

variants.name: Run selector (TensorBoard / W&B)
variants.thesis: The rail IS the rows: datasets as groups with a colour and a three-state checkbox, their trajectories under them, a regex box, Split and Kind as toggles that apply to every dataset ticked; every figure is coloured and split by dataset.
variants.bestWhen: Comparing datasets is the point: the headline numbers come as one row per dataset plus "All shown", and every map has a row per dataset in its colour (with a Together switch).
variants.losesWhen: Many datasets (past about 6 the rows grow and data-ui has 8 series colours); embedded, the Overview's third section starts below the fold; it adds the most new data-ui API.

variants.name: A filter scope; the host composes
variants.thesis: No monolith: data-ui adds one context element, <data-scope>, and every data-ui element inside it — facets, a <data-tabs> strip, dashboards, a table — shares its rows and its one filter; the host lays the parts out however its app needs.
variants.bestWhen: Different apps need different layouts of the same parts: the full TensorBoard layout, a compact embed, or a card inside robotparts' datasheet (card.html shows two independent scopes on one page).
variants.losesWhen: Embedded, the active filter folds into a "Filters · N" chip, so the picks themselves aren't visible on the tab; each app writes its own few lines of layout; five small new elements to land.
